label: D1 spike after S1-rewarded trial followed by a2->S2 switch, stronger if unrewarded
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u")
explanation: Sparse D1-only feature (nonzero on 1.7% of steps, zero at GO/D2), rising across the episode. Its magnitude is set by the last two trials: it fires at D1 when the previous trial reached S2 and the trial before reached S1, i.e. a state switch S1 -> S2. The largest activations come when the trial two back was S1 rewarded (mostly a1 S1 r; a2 S1 r is somewhat weaker) and the previous trial was a2 -> S2 (fitted about +0.33). It is larger again if that S2 trial was unrewarded (+0.11) and grows a little later in the episode. The S1 r -> a1 S2 (rare) path and a plain S1 -> S2 sequence give smaller effects. After a previous S1 trial it stays near zero. All terms are observed history; no future, hidden or model-output variables were used. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.24, test 0.24. That is above the profile all-cue additive ceiling (0.17), because the effect is a two-trial conjunction. Most of the variance in the rare large spikes is still unexplained.
